summary.text: Jerusalem was the capital of Judea under its Herodian client kings and, throughout the first century AD, the religious center of Judaism as the site of the Second Temple; the Gospels set Jesus' final days, death, and resurrection appearances there.

history.text: By the time of Herod the Great, Jerusalem had grown well beyond its earlier Old Testament boundaries, and Herod's building program, including the enlarged Temple platform, made it one of the major cities of the eastern Roman world.
Roman forces under Titus destroyed the city and the Second Temple in AD 70 during the First Jewish-Roman War, an event referenced elsewhere in the New Testament as a coming judgment.
